correctness.summary: Generalized Dixmier averaging gives T_M(J)⊂J and lifts every central quotient element to the center modulo J. Wang's theorem then turns every element of the descended trace kernel into one commutator, while traciality gives the converse. The exact distance formula follows from contractivity of the descended idempotent. The reduced-product sharp-K estimate was checked using the ideal quotient norm formula and coordinatewise balancing of the two commutator factors.

limitations: The descended central tracial projection can be nonfaithful.
The generic quotient estimate is 2K and is not claimed optimal.
Properly infinite von Neumann algebras are not covered.
The sharp-K refinement is proved for the stated norm reduced products of finite-dimensional C*-algebras.
Older or poorly indexed center-quotient and commutator literature may contain equivalent special cases.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The classical Dixmier/center-lifting mechanism and quotient-norm formula are treated as prior art. Searches around arXiv:2609.16932, finite-von-Neumann quotients, closed ideals, center-valued traces, single commutators, reduced products and matrix coronas did not locate the combined theorem for arbitrary operator-norm quotients, its exact distance formula, or the positive-projection corona consequence. Older center-quotient or abstract commutator literature remains a residual bibliographic risk.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result turns the single-commutator image in every norm-closed quotient of a finite von Neumann algebra into a closed linear subspace with an exact metric formula. It also preserves the new universal commutator constant in norm reduced products and exhibits nonzero positive projections that are single additive commutators in the matrix corona.
